purpose: Every relation in authorization-model-v1.fga, with what it is expected to allow and to deny. The completeness gate refuses a model relation that is absent here, so a new relation cannot land without someone stating what it must not reach.

relations.allows: A named user is part of a team, so team-granted product roles reach them.
relations.denies: Nothing on its own. Membership is not access; it only carries whatever the product grants the team.

relations.allows: Read the cases of one org, once derived into case_viewer.
relations.denies: Any other org — the object is ethics_product:<orgId>, so a grant cannot span tenants. Also denies writing: viewer never derives case_handler.

relations.allows: Route and assign cases in one org (case_triager), and read them (case_viewer).
relations.denies: Other orgs; and handling — triager does not derive case_handler.

relations.allows: Reply on cases in one org (case_handler) and read them (case_viewer).
relations.denies: Other orgs; and triage — handler does not derive case_triager.

relations.allows: Operate the product without reading its content.
relations.denies: Every content relation. technical_admin IS content_denied, which subtracts from case_viewer, case_triager, case_handler and evidence_reveal_approved. An operator who can restart the service still cannot open a report.

relations.allows: Approve a reveal of sealed evidence (evidence_reveal_approved).
relations.denies: Reading cases — evidence_approver alone derives no case_viewer. Approving is not the same authority as reading.

relations.allows: Administer product membership for one org.
relations.denies: Case content. It derives none of the case_* relations — administering who may read is separate from reading.

relations.allows: Nothing. It exists only to be subtracted.
relations.denies: case_viewer, case_triager, case_handler and evidence_reveal_approved, regardless of any other grant the same principal holds.

relations.derivation: (viewer or triager or handler) but not content_denied
relations.allows: List and open the cases of one org. This is what EthicsAuthorization.can() asks for on every staff read.
relations.denies: A technical_admin, even one who also holds viewer. The subtraction wins.

relations.allows: Assign a case.
relations.denies: Anyone holding only viewer or handler, and any technical_admin.

relations.allows: Reply to the reporter and write internal notes.
relations.denies: Anyone holding only viewer or triager, and any technical_admin.

relations.allows: Approve revealing sealed evidence.
relations.denies: Anyone who is not an evidence_approver, and any technical_admin.

relations.allows: A named user or team may be trusted to approve revealing who a report is about. Assignable on its own, so the circle can be smaller than the set of people handling cases.
relations.denies: Deliberately NOT derived from handler or triager. Handling a case must not by itself reveal the identity of the person it names — nothing has been established about them yet, and the product protects them as well as the reporter. Holding every other product role grants nothing here.

relations.allows: Effective subject-reveal approval at product level: subject_approver minus content_denied.
relations.denies: Operators. An account that can run the system is subtracted here exactly as it is from case content, so administering the platform never becomes a way to learn who was reported.

relations.allows: Binds one case to one product, which is how the per-org grants reach it.
relations.denies: Cross-tenant reach. A case bound to one product cannot be reached through another.

relations.allows: Nothing. Like content_denied it exists only to subtract.
relations.denies: Every case_* relation on that one case, for that one principal, whatever the product grants. Recorded by an authorized party about someone else.

relations.allows: Nothing. Subtractive, same as conflicted, but self-declared (ES-203, POST /cases/{id}/recusal).
relations.denies: Every case_* relation on that one case for the declaring principal. Once written the case leaves their view, so the same person cannot reach it again — a second declaration answers 404.

relations.allows: Nothing.
relations.denies: Whatever either input denies. One subtraction is enough; they are not required together.

relations.derivation: case_viewer from product but not denied
relations.allows: Open one specific case.
relations.denies: A conflicted or recused principal, even one whose product membership is intact. Refusal is a 404 rather than a 403, so it does not confirm the case exists.

relations.derivation: case_triager from product but not denied
relations.allows: Assign one specific case.
relations.denies: A conflicted or recused principal — the exclusion the ES-203 acceptance names for triagers.

relations.derivation: case_handler from product but not denied
relations.allows: Reply on one specific case.
relations.denies: A conflicted or recused principal — the exclusion for assignees.

relations.derivation: evidence_reveal_approved from product but not denied
relations.allows: Approve a reveal on one specific case.
relations.denies: A conflicted or recused approver — the exclusion for reveal approvers, so an interested party cannot approve unsealing evidence about themselves.

relations.derivation: subject_reveal_approved from product but not denied
relations.allows: Effective subject-reveal approval on one case, inherited through the product.
relations.denies: Anyone conflicted or recused on that case, through the same `denied` subtraction every positive case relation carries. Stepping away from a case removes subject access with it.
